overall_status: conditional_binary_electrolyte_flux_identity_and_nonidentifiability; prior art preempts generic nanopore Peltier cooling; physical flux attribution and device efficiency unknown

claims.exact_statement: For signed monovalent cation and anion molar fluxes J_plus,J_minus along one axis, current density I=F(J_plus-J_minus), neutral salt flux J_s=(J_plus+J_minus)/2, and constant species heats of transport Q_plus,Q_minus, ionic heat flux J_Q=Q_plus J_plus+Q_minus J_minus equals ((Q_plus-Q_minus)/(2F)) I +(Q_plus+Q_minus)J_s. If Q_plus+Q_minus is nonzero, current alone does not identify J_Q; adding the same flux a to both species preserves I and changes J_Q by (Q_plus+Q_minus)a.
assumptions: One-dimensional signed species molar fluxes for a binary 1:1 electrolyte.
Constant heats of transport Q_plus and Q_minus in the admitted model.
Ionic advective/transport heat is defined as the species sum Q_plus J_plus + Q_minus J_minus; solvent advection, electrode reaction heat, and Fourier conduction are separate channels.
claims.status: internally_derived_exact_model_identity_and_identifiability_obstruction; no nature-level validation; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: The algebra is elementary and follows the established heat-of-transport framework. The scoped contribution is applying its nullspace counterexample to the current-plus-local-temperature interface of a gated salt-gradient nanopore; no priority is claimed.
claims.costs: Acquiring J_s or both species fluxes, maintaining/assaying activities and concentration reservoirs, measuring local heat flux/thermal conductance, calibrating Q_i, resolving solvent flow and electrode heat, and fabricating calibrated nanothermocouple-gated pores.
claims.falsifier: Under the stated flux definitions, an exact arithmetic counterexample to the identity would falsify the derivation. For a physical transfer, failure of independently measured heat flux to match the constant-Q_i model after accounting for salt flux and other heat channels rejects that model transfer, not the identity.
claims.next_gate: At fixed pore and gradient, measure signed Na and Cl flux or J_s simultaneously with current and heat flux under preregistered bias/gate/gradient reversals; compare the held-out flux using equation (1).

claims.exact_statement: Using the 2025 source-reported Q_Na=3.5 kJ/mol and Q_Cl=0.5 kJ/mol, the same 1 microamp current has ionic heat flux 36.27 nW for ideal Na-only flux and 15.55 nW for zero-salt-flux counterflow; the difference is 20.73 nW. At 293 K, an ideal 10^4 monovalent activity ratio gives a Nernst voltage magnitude 0.23255 V, while an ideal neutral NaCl formula-unit chemical-potential difference is 44.88 kJ/mol.
assumptions: Source-reported heats of transport apply unchanged to the two idealized flux states.
Ideal activities for the Nernst/chemical-potential figures; actual 1.4 M solution nonideality is not accounted for.
The same-current comparison is a model witness, not a claim that either flux state was measured in the 2025 device.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/c9_energy_thermal_ions/FINAL_REPORT.md, Numerical prediction; values recomputed directly from F=96485.33212 C/mol and R=8.31446261815324 J/(mol K)
claims.novelty_boundary: A unit conversion and conditional counterexample, not a new material measurement or priority result.
claims.costs: No new measured inputs beyond the cited Q_i values, ideal-activity assumption, temperature, and selected current scale; actual transfer requires species-flux and activity measurements.
claims.falsifier: Measured heats of transport or ionic fluxes differing from the supplied model invalidate this numerical prediction for that specimen; they do not invalidate the flux identity.
claims.next_gate: Measure species flux and local heat flux under the source geometry; test whether the predicted per-current ambiguity is physically occupied in the operating window.

claims.exact_statement: Generic Peltier cooling by charge-selective nanopore ion transport is already source-reported in Tsutsui et al., Device 2 (2024), DOI 10.1016/j.device.2023.100188. The 2025 ACS Nano paper's narrower reported addition is field-effect control/reversal and its specific integrated gate/thermocouple geometry; it is not the first demonstration of nanopore ionic cooling.
assumptions: Prior-art comparison is limited to the full primary 2024 Device paper and 2025 ACS Nano paper inspected here.
The status is about published statement overlap, not a complete global novelty search.
claims.novelty_boundary: No priority claim; this is a bounded overlap audit. The earlier work already reports the central ionic Peltier-cooling mechanism and Seebeck/Peltier reciprocity.
claims.costs: Primary article reading only; the full global citation/claim search and independent reproduction are not complete.
claims.falsifier: A scope mismatch in the cited 2024 primary source would alter the bounded prior-art statement; it would not change the 2025 paper's reported device data.
claims.next_gate: If prioritizing the architecture, compare the exact externally gated sign-reversal/control law against prior gate-all-around nanopore and nanofluidic thermoelectric literature beyond the bounded audit here.
